about: The options that force or forbid others, for the closure pass (judging/closure/README.md). A row that matches 'if' must match 'then'. Sources: SPACE section 5 (the arrows read 'forces'), the 'needs' of SPACE section 2, AMENDMENTS sections 2 and 4, and the tags whose SPACE footnote ties them to their row's other options. Each says why the two options cannot work together; none rules a row out for being weak.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: R isr forces C cent
constraints.why: The in-sync set is changed by someone outside the group. cent-co is cent run as a loop by #meta's leader (its precedent is KRaft's combined mode), so it is outside the group too and is allowed.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: R slog, obj (and rlog) force V tier
constraints.why: Durability lives off the servers, on the log nodes or in the object store.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: R rlog forces V tier, with servers as learners; SPACE footnote 9
constraints.why: The log members are the voters; servers are learners that fold, and the writer is a server holding a writer epoch.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: R not raft, I applies only to a metadata group
constraints.why: The data groups do not run Raft, so a Raft core can only serve the metadata group (or there is none).

constraints.source: SPACE 2 I: the Raft core, when some group runs Raft
constraints.why: The data groups run Raft, so the row needs a Raft core for them; port(meta) is Raft for metadata only, and '-' is none.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: R lww, X at most saga without fences
constraints.why: Leaderless writes have no single writer to judge against, so no 2pc or ktxn coordinator can hold.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: P slot forces O slot (or hlc)
constraints.why: Offsets and per-group state do not survive a slot move.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: P split forces O off+lin or hlc
constraints.why: Children inherit the parent's offsets, so a position needs the lineage or a timestamp.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: X 2pc forces a multi-version S (lsm)
constraints.why: Readers need a snapshot timestamp, so the store must keep several versions.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: X 2pc forces O hlc or T tso
constraints.why: Readers need a snapshot timestamp: hybrid-logical-clock positions or a timestamp oracle.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: Q maj-m needs rejoin-as-new; AMENDMENTS 2 Q (mix holds maj-m)
constraints.why: Under the memory rung a disk may lack what it acknowledged, so a replica that stopped uncleanly must come back as new. Z crash has no such rule. Z par keeps the incarnation (disk-incarnation). V4's mix is its own ladder (R lww), so it is not named.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: V +wit needs an object store to repair (S +tier)
constraints.why: A log replica cannot build a full replica from its log alone.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: F ldr removes follower state reads (W any for logs only)
constraints.why: Followers hold no state, so state reads cannot come from any replica. OBJ's ldr + lazy is not named: its lazy followers fold on read.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: H side forces U ldr
constraints.why: The app folds only what its host leads, so calls go to the leader's host.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: H side forces F ldr in the app, logs in the daemon; SPACE footnote 11
constraints.why: The daemon keeps the logs; the app's Node process folds for the groups its host leads.

constraints.source: SPACE 5 and SPACE 2 N pool: pool needs isolates (L rs+v8)
constraints.why: Many projects share a process, so user code must run in isolates.

constraints.source: SPACE 5: U cli or L rs-srv, no JS on servers; SPACE 2 L rs-srv
constraints.why: A Rust or Go server runs no JS unless it embeds an engine (rs+v8), so methods cannot run on servers: apps are clients.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 Q isr: needs R isr
constraints.why: A commit at every member of the in-sync set needs an in-sync set.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 Q put: needs R obj
constraints.why: A commit that is a PUT needs the object store as the log.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 S obj: needs R obj
constraints.why: The object store only, with a local cache, holds the log only when the object store is the log.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 D txn: needs X 2pc
constraints.why: Transaction ids are dedup under two-phase commit.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 V tier: comes with R slog, obj or rlog
constraints.why: A separate log tier holds all durability only under a log-first R.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 I raft-rs: needs L rs+napi (a Rust L)
constraints.why: raft-rs is Rust. SPACE names rs+napi; SRV, PD, EMB-V8 and SIDE run it natively in a Rust server, so any Rust L holds.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 I port: port etcd's raft to TS; raft-rs later
constraints.why: The port is a TypeScript Raft core; a row whose core is Rust from day one (rs+napi, a Rust server) cannot run it.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 G pslot: a group holds (resource, slot set) pairs; '0 beyond P slot'
constraints.why: Project groups are made of slot sets, so the row needs slots.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 G lane; SPACE 4.1 LANE (P fixN (lanes))
constraints.why: A fixed number of logs per project that every resource hashes into: the lanes are the mapping.

constraints.source: AMENDMENTS 2 N: 'with V +lrn and H emb there is no log tier to pool, so N follows V'; SPACE 4.1: tier where the row has log replicas
constraints.why: Only the log tier is pooled, so the row needs log replicas or a log tier to pool.

constraints.source: AMENDMENTS 2 H: 'both is emb plus log members; it is needed only with V +wit or N tier'
constraints.why: Log replicas and log tiers are processes of their own; fero inside the app's process alone (H emb) has none.

constraints.source: AMENDMENTS 2 P: who decides the moves under C self is undecided, in two forms (the loop of self+mv, or each leader's rule of P slot + rule); A-18: in cent and cent-co rows the mover is the controller; AMENDMENTS 4 footnotes 14, 15
constraints.why: Plain slots under plain self have no mover: nobody runs A-18's policy. self+p is allowed: its planner sends move hints that take the move lease like any mover.

constraints.source: AMENDMENTS 4 footnotes 14 and 15; axes.json tag note for C self+mv
constraints.why: self+mv is self plus one loop on #meta's leader that only proposes slot moves; with no slots the loop has nothing to move.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 C cent-co: a loop run by #meta's leader; AMENDMENTS 4 (self+mv's loop on #meta's leader)
constraints.why: The loop runs on the leader of the metadata Raft group, so the row needs some Raft group (I not '-').

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 5 (SLOG)
constraints.why: The writer changes its log nodes and the controller changes writers: loglet writers exist only under slog.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 7 (OBJ)
constraints.why: CAS on the object store's manifest: the manifest is the object log's.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 6 (SLOG)
constraints.why: A write quorum of the log nodes: log nodes exist only under slog.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 4 (ISR, SLOG)
constraints.why: Raft for the metadata group only: the data groups do not run Raft, and the row has a metadata group.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 3 (LEAN); AMENDMENTS A-26
constraints.why: One warm standby that folds is a choice only where the other followers do not fold.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 9 (RLOG)
constraints.why: Log members vote, servers are full learners, the writer holds a writer epoch: that is rlog.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 9 (RLOG)
constraints.why: Servers fold and log members do not: the split of roles is rlog's.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 10 (EMB-V8)
constraints.why: data folds inside V8 isolates in the server, which only rs+v8 embeds.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 11 (SIDE)
constraints.why: The app's Node process folds for the groups its host leads: that app sits beside a daemon.

constraints.source: SPACE 4.1 SIDE: fwd (to the local daemon)
constraints.why: Writes go to the local daemon, which only H side has.

constraints.source: SPACE 4.1 SIDE; SPACE 2 H side
constraints.why: A native daemon plus the app's TypeScript is the side split.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 H side: a native daemon per host; the app's Node process runs rules, methods and data's fold
constraints.why: The daemon is native and the app is TypeScript.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 2 (SRV)
constraints.why: The server folds plain rows in Rust and data's views run on clients: the library lives in a native server.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 2 (SRV)
constraints.why: The server folds plain rows in Rust; data's views run on clients and relays.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 8 (SRV)
constraints.why: Two variants of one row: Rust with raft-rs, or Go with etcd's raft run natively.

constraints.source: SPACE footnote 8 (SRV)
constraints.why: Two variants of one row: the Go variant runs etcd's raft natively, the Rust one raft-rs.

constraints.source: SPACE 4.1 LANE: fixN (lanes)
constraints.why: N fixed lanes per project is the lane option's own mapping.

constraints.source: SPACE 4.1 SLOG (S tier + obj); SPACE 2 V tier
constraints.why: The log tier holds the log and the object store the rest, so the row needs a separate log tier.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 L rs-srv (a Rust server, a TS client) and rs+v8 (a Rust server that embeds V8); SPACE 2 H emb, side
constraints.why: A native server binary cannot run inside the app's Node process (emb), and side's native part is a daemon beside the app (L rs-srv + ts).

constraints.source: SPACE 2 U cli (no user code on servers; apps are clients) and H srv (apps are clients)
constraints.why: Under emb, both or side the app's own process runs fero and its code, so apps are not clients.

constraints.source: SPACE 4.1 BUY (L ts client) and footnote 12
constraints.why: fero as a TS client only exists on top of an outside log; with a log of fero's own there is a kernel to build. The search leaves R outside out, so this keeps BUY's L tag out of it too.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 R obj: 'a commit is a PUT'
constraints.why: Q says what a commit means; under R obj it is the PUT.

constraints.source: SPACE 2 R obj: 'the object store is the durable layer'
constraints.why: The store holds the log; servers keep only a cache (S obj).
